knows: Elements occupy rows and columns in the periodic table.
doesNotKnow: Potassium’s outer electron is in a higher shell; its first ionization energy is lower than sodium’s.

misconception: First ionization energy increases without any exceptions across every period.
objective: Compare first ionization energies while recognizing the stated periodic exceptions.

claims.text: Question, diagram and explanation: Among neutral, isolated gas-phase atoms of Na and K, which has the higher first ionization energy? Na has the higher first ionization energy. Potassium’s outer electron is in a higher shell; its first ionization energy is lower than sodium’s. First ionization energy is the energy required to remove the first electron from an isolated gaseous atom.
